assertion.objects: The actual finite coefficient module with action R(g)=theta(g)rho_T(g), G_K and open G_Hf, and the left-coset representatives used in H21.
assertion.hypotheses: theta factors through the finite ring-class quotient, so its restriction to G_Hf is trivial; the finite Tate coefficient action is continuous; sections are transported consistently.
assertion.quantifiers: Every such open subgroup and coefficient module, all cochain degrees and compatible towers.
assertion.parameter_range: Integral coefficient modules; finite-index open subgroups, without invertibility of the index.
assertion.uniformity: Natural cochain constructions and section-change homotopies; no quantitative bound.
assertion.constants: No averaging factor or division by the subgroup index.
assertion.normalizations: Use left representatives g r_delta=r_(g delta) h(g,delta), with the actual R(r) weight and the ordinary inhomogeneous differential.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No averaging, no new infinite-order character, and no automatic local-condition compatibility; the local diagrams are separately constructed.
assertion.limit_order: Choose the modules and sections, form cochain maps and their homotopies, then pass to cohomology.
assertion.statement: The actual weighted transfer in H21 and its degree-n version are integral cochain maps; changing sections gives an integral homotopy, and compatible sections give strictly transitive transfer.

use.reason: Exact integral transfer input into the retained cochain construction.

supplier.statement: The Shapiro map from the induced continuous-cochain complex to the subgroup cochain complex is a quasi-isomorphism; integral finite-sum corestriction is a chain map, independent of section up to the explicit homotopy, and transitive for compatible sections.
